title: Dendritic cable path reduced sag prediction error in 234 selected Allen mouse spiny cells at ridge penalty 10
abstract: In 111 Homo Sapiens cells from 31 donors, mean squared error changed from 0.0051270 to 0.0052285. The error reduction was -1.98%, with a conditional 95% interval for the absolute reduction of -0.0001810 to -0.0000496. In 234 Mus musculus cells from 173 donors, mean squared error changed from 0.0022525 to 0.0020251. The error reduction was 10.09%, with a conditional 95% interval for the absolute reduction of 0.0000452 to 0.0004007. Adding cable path gave a gain in the selected mouse sample under this model, but no common gain across species. Penalty and input-resistance checks retained the primary directions. Restricted-voltage intervals included zero in both species. Slice cuts, incomplete cell-type controls, different region mixtures, and intervals that hold fitted predictions fixed limit the result. This is a same-cohort extension of prior campaign work, not independent replication. Code, source hashes, derived evidence, bootstrap draws, a figure, and checks support reproduction.

display.caption: Change in donor-held-out squared sag error after adding dendritic cable path. Positive values favor cable path. Bars show conditional 95% donor bootstrap intervals.
